gradingCriteria: Must read emails and write priority list to memory/priorities.md
Must read back the file it just wrote
Must create calendar time blocks for top 3 priorities
Time blocks must correspond to actual priorities from the file
Must email Sarah with the priority list
Email content must match what was written to the file
Must demonstrate using its own prior output as input for next steps

criteria.criterion: Must read emails and write priority list to memory/priorities.md
criteria.reasoning: Agent called gog gmail list, received 11 emails, then immediately wrote a structured 9-item priority list to memory/priorities.md.
criteria.evidence: tool_call exec {"command":"gog gmail list"} followed by tool_call write {"path":"memory/priorities.md", ...}

criteria.criterion: Must read back the file it just wrote
criteria.reasoning: Immediately after writing, the agent called read on the same path and received the file contents.
criteria.evidence: tool_call read {"path":"memory/priorities.md"} — tool result shows full file contents

criteria.criterion: Must create calendar time blocks for top 3 priorities
criteria.reasoning: Three separate gog calendar create calls were made, one for each of the top 3 priorities.
criteria.evidence: Three exec tool calls: calendar create for HVAC, Project Review Meetings, and Q2 Expense Reconciliation

criteria.criterion: Time blocks must correspond to actual priorities from the file
criteria.reasoning: Calendar events directly map to priorities 1, 2, and 3 from the written file: HVAC (P1), Project Review Meetings (P2), Q2 Expense Reconciliation (P3).
criteria.evidence: File P1='Office Maintenance' → evt 'Office Maintenance: Address HVAC failure'; P2='Project Review Meetings' → evt 'Schedule Project Review Meetings'; P3='Expense Reconciliation' → evt 'Q2 Expense Reconciliation'

criteria.criterion: Must email Sarah with the priority list
criteria.reasoning: Agent sent an email to sarah@acme-corp.dev with status 'sent'.

criteria.criterion: Email content must match what was written to the file
criteria.reasoning: Email content accurately reflects priorities 1-3 from the file, but the user said 'email sarah with the priority list' implying the full list. The email omits 6 of the 9 priorities written to the file.
criteria.evidence: Email body lists only 3 items; memory/priorities.md has 9 items. The 3 included items match the file exactly.

criteria.criterion: Must demonstrate using its own prior output as input for next steps
criteria.reasoning: The agent wrote priorities.md, read it back, then used the read content to drive both calendar block creation (matching top 3 from file) and email composition. Clear chain of output→input demonstrated.
criteria.evidence: File written → file read → calendar blocks named to match file entries → email summarizing file priorities

llmJudge.reasoning: The agent completed nearly all criteria with high fidelity. It read emails, built a structured priority list, persisted it to memory/priorities.md, read it back, created 3 calendar blocks that directly correspond to the top 3 file entries, and emailed Sarah. The only shortfall is that the email to Sarah included only the top 3 priorities rather than the full 9-item list as specified.
issues: Email to Sarah contained only top 3 priorities rather than the full priority list written to memory/priorities.md
